sites.name: Fort Garland Military Post & Museum Complex
overview: Fort Garland is a surviving nineteenth-century U.S. Army post in Colorado's San Luis Valley. Built in 1858 after the earlier Fort Massachusetts proved poorly located, it served as a regional military base until 1883.
The historic site retains original adobe buildings and is interpreted today as the Fort Garland Museum & Cultural Center.

timeline.text: The Army established Fort Garland on the San Luis Valley floor after relocating from Fort Massachusetts.
Kit Carson commanded Fort Garland during this period.
The U.S. Army abandoned Fort Garland after roughly twenty-five years of operation.

moreHistory: History Colorado identifies Fort Garland as important to the settlement of the San Luis Valley and southern Colorado, while National Park Service history places the post within the region's Civil War-era and later military landscape.
Original buildings and artifacts survive at the state historic site, making the fort complex itself a stable identification feature rather than relying on a reconstructed or approximate location.
